user.title: Configure Cube Charger
user.description: Enter portal URL, Bearer token and idTag→car mapping. Example: RFID_VW:VW, RFID_PEU:Peugeot

data_description.car_connected_entity: Optional — leave empty to skip. Fill in a car-side "plugged in" entity (e.g. a binary_sensor from your car's own HA integration) if you want the evcc status sensor to report 'B' (connected, not charging) instead of only 'A'/'C'. Accepted states: on, true, 1, connected, plugged_in or yes (case-insensitive); any binary_sensor/switch/input_boolean or plain sensor with one of those states works. Without it, status stays 'A' until a session starts.
data_description.car_max_current_entity: Optional — leave empty to skip. Fill in a car-side number or input_number entity (e.g. from your car's own HA integration) that actually limits charging current, if you want evcc's requested max current to really be applied to the car — not just stored locally. Must accept number.set_value / input_number.set_value calls in amperes; its min/max/step are copied over at startup. Without it, number.cube_charger_max_current still exists (evcc requires it) but changes have no real effect.
data_description.webhook_secret: Optional, but strongly recommended once you've found it. Every Cube webhook call includes an X-CubeSignature header (HMAC-SHA256 over the raw payload). Set the matching secret here so incoming events get verified — without it, events are still processed (the webhook URL itself is already hard to guess), but anyone who learns the URL could in theory send fake status/energy events.
